fullPassage: It is important to recognize that although science is a rule-based procedure, it is very much a creative process. ( ① ) A conjecture is a philosophical invention, cooked up rather mystically by the mind through the mental computation we call careful contemplation. ( ② ) However, until the hypothesis is tested against reality, it is not yet truly knowledge; it is just information that represents speculation. ( ③ ) Knowledge is information that has demonstrated its usefulness. It is what is left over after cycles of experimental testing have eliminated false theories. ( ④ ) As scientists continually test their hypotheses and modify their models to account for new and surprising data, a kind of 'learning loop' emerges that statisticians call Bayesian updating. Based on Bayes' Rule, developed by eighteenth-century English statistician and philosopher Thomas Bayes, Bayesian updating refers to a mathematical process whereby an accepted theory or predictive model gets increasingly accurate through the repetitive testing of competing variants of that theory.
